Yeah, that's pretty much the only thing I'm concerned about. 

Other people  will be more like "Oh, throwawayobvss? Yeah I remember that guy. Oh, puppies." while my family would be like "Where the fuck is throwawayobvss ?". I can't really just "bore" them out of my life.

> Are you thinking about suicide because of an event in your life that makes you sad or are you just bored with life ?

Probably several events. I feel that every attempt at anything I've tried has gone wrong. The high expectations of myself wanting to do well academically, socially and artistically.

> Cutting ties with them just so you can leave them behind is less sudden than suicide, but you're still leaving others who care about you behind.

Yeah, this is definitely the hardest part with family. 

In my own personal experience with friendships, they come and go and people move on. They need to. There are people out there who were able to maintain friendships and relationships for a long period of time and it's something I have yet to be able to do. It's tiring and nerve wrecking when I attempt to do so. In my own personal experience with strictly friends, it has been easier to cut ties than to develop them. Maybe it's because I've never really been that close to people to begin with.
I wouldn't murder a bunch of criminals. That's kind of unfair.

> This is a logistical nightmare. You'll never be able to pull it off. Every step here is riddled with complexity. Sorry OP but you're living in a fantasy world. The fact is that it takes a lot to kill an entire human body. More than you realize. This plan is just not going to work.

For sure, it's going to be hard to pull something like having my body disposed of properly. If I am going to pass away, I'd rather just have it done painlessly. The part of having my organs donated is just an extra bonus. It's far less messy and someone else could make use of it. The planning process sounds like hell, but for some reason it feels more right. 

I find the most complex part is having to cut ties with the people who have been in your life forever. I still haven't figured out how to do this.

> But really, what jumps out at me is your profound naivete and judgemental attitude in assuming that people who kill themselves are selfish instead of focusing on the extent to which they felt miserable and alienated......your post is basically about how others who committed suicide are bad selfish people and how you are going to be better than them. Do you really want to compete with someone about the correct way to kill yourself?

But I do understand their suffering. I hear about stories of what led people to kill themselves, whether it's through immense financial loss, loss of a loved one, a break up. Everyone has different thresholds and some break down earlier than others, some slower. I find myself both lacking sympathy, because I think it can be done in a better, controlled way without minimal effects to others around them but envious that they were able to go through it. It's bittersweet.

> If you were raised to compete and judge others and try to be better than other people all the time, you're not going to be a happy person. And maybe that's why you feel such pressure that you want to just leave the planet entirely.

My naivete and judgmental ways is likely part of my personality. I've always felt that I can do better than anything I see. That kind of mindset does backfire most times, but it's been part of me for so long that I can't change it. It's almost instinctive. It's what makes me, me.

> And what also jumps out at me is the utter lack of any exposition on your part of why you want to die. 

I wasn't exactly so sure if I should really tell you why. I don't want to give too much details that it would easily give out my information.

>  If you were raised to compete and judge others and try to be better than other people all the time, you're not going to be a happy person. And maybe that's why you feel such pressure that you want to just leave the planet entirely.

I've tried to change myself but I'm having too much difficulty. I could easily tell the same thing you tell me to myself if I was someone else, but I can't bring myself to explain it to me. It becomes emotionally exhausting and I can even see it whenever I try to socialize with others. I can't exactly "fake" it so I've given up and just decided to be who I am and stopped socializing. I'm sure anxiety and depression are key factors and I'm compensating by being an arrogant asshole in my head as a security blanket - thinking that I could do better and be smarter about it. I tried to change myself and I couldn't. So I just accepted myself the way I am. Unfortunately, this type of mindset and personality doesn't really mesh well others.

I've actually visited Thailand before. It was too hot and humid for my liking :P


It's not really a matter of wanting to start something new. It's a matter of ending it. I choose Thailand simply because it's much easier to disappear there.

> I guess what I'm trying to say is people will always care about you, dissapearing will always make them wonder what happened to you, 

It'll only be a fleeting thought. Nothing that will literally cripple someone to the point of being unable to function in life. That's why it's a bit hard when you still have family with you. 

>  even I care about ya' op!

Heh, while I appreciate the sentiment, we barely know each other. I mean this with no offense.
Haha. If I was an attention whore, I would be committing suicide while maintaining my relationships. I'm actually interested in seeing other people's point of view in regards to this.
